sentences.text:
This is third application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.88/2021 dated 21.03.2021 registered at Police Station- Ghansore, District- Seoni, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 344, 376,
376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and 3, 4, 5 & 6 of POCSO Act.
His earlier two applications for bail were dismissed vide order dated 11.11.2021 and 26.07.2022 respectively.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 05.08.2021.
The applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He further submits that prosecutrix was consenting party, as she eloped with the applicant on her own volition.
She visited various places with the applicant on her own will.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.

Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be released on bail.
On the contrary, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.

According to prosecution's case, this is the third bail application of the applicant in light of the fact that his second bail application was decided in M.Cr.C. No.23176/2022, which was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to revive the prayer after examination of prosecutrix, her parents and other material witnesses.
Statements of prosecutrix, her mother and her relatives have been filed along with the present application.
Admittedly, prosecutrix had completed age of 17 years when incident occurred.

Prosecution story also suggests that she stayed with the applicant for atleast 5 months and she traveled with him to various places and never raised alarm about the sexual advances being made by the applicant.
Still her statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. and also before the trial Court consistently disclose that she was forced to have sexual relationship by the applicant.
Looking to the age of prosecutrix and her consistent statements recorded before the various authorities, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail on behalf of applicant stands rejected.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE pnm Subhash Chandra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23101676/
